answer_1.quote: The agent initializes this model given task description, using pre-trained knowledge in VLMs to infer precise, task-relevant contents written as structured texts. The agent then makes explicit plans by specifying a rule-based policy written as executable code... Given the world model and visual observations, we prompt the VLM to generate a Python function to address the task.
answer_1.outputs: Executable Python code for action plans and text-based world model graphs

answer_2.quote: For the MobileAgentBench tasks, we adopted the six metrics originally introduced in the corresponding paper: • Success Rate (SR): SR = Nsuccess M tasks , measuring the proportion of tasks successfully completed. • Step-wise Efficiency (SE): SE = S actual S optimal , assessing unnecessary/redundant actions... • Latency: Average seconds between consecutive user actions... • Tokens: Counts input and output tokens processed by the VLM... • False Negative (FN)... • False Positive (FP)... In our real-world evaluations, we concentrate exclusively on the most critical metrics... • Success Rate (SR)... • Completion Rate (CR): CR = Scorrect S total...
